key.name: window-rules
key.summary: Where the automatic decoration is reversed, per window kind
key.description: Window kinds this extension decorates, and where the user reversed the automatic decision. Keyed by a window-kind fingerprint: '<identity>:client_type=<wayland|x11>,window_type=<int>,has_parent=<bool>,allows_resize=<bool>,attached_dialog=<bool>,has_ring=<bool>,has_ssd=<bool>'. A fixed-size window (allows_resize=false) may add ',size=<W>x<H>' in logical pixels to tell apart dialogs of one application that otherwise share a fingerprint; a rule without it still matches them. For example, 'wechat:client_type=wayland,window_type=0,has_parent=true,allows_resize=false,attached_dialog=false,has_ring=false,has_ssd=false'. The fingerprint is derived from the picked window's stable structural attributes, so a rule never generalizes to every window of an application. The state names the axes whose automatic decision is reversed, in canonical order, e.g. 'corners,shadow'; an axis not named follows the automatic decision, and a state naming nothing is the same as no rule. The resize axis is about the grab band, and reversing it is bidirectional: it widens the band to the native 12 pixels out on every side, and 24 along the edge at each corner, or retracts the band the reading drew; a GTK4 window declaring at least 12 pixels on every side already owns a native-width handle, so the heuristic leaves it alone. Structural facts (non-decorable window type, maximized/fullscreen, unresizable windows, SSD frames) are capability, not choice, and a reversed axis never overrides them.

key.name: prefer-crisp-text
key.description: Skip rounded corners on fractional scale monitors (retaining shadow) to avoid text blur and resampling overhead.
